Filtering rows with WHERE

Unit 2 · Week 4 · Lesson 2 · Suggested 55-minute plan; adjust to local timing.

Prepare: Open a working copy of sql-starter.sqlite in a school-approved SQLite-capable application and locate its SQL editor. Alternatively execute sql-setup.sql once in a new empty database. Run one SELECT at a time. Use sql-workbook.md, sql-answers.md, sql-worked-queries.sql and sql-expected-results.json. The data are fictional. DueDate is valid YYYY-MM-DD TEXT and Returned is INTEGER 0/1 in this SQLite starter. Fixed reporting date: 8 April 2026. Teacher notes and answers are public.

Suggested answers are teacher guidance, not extra assessment tasks. These notes are public.

1. Filtering rows with WHERE

Suggested time: 2 minutes

Instructional strategy: Learning intention

Return to the earlier single-item Loan model. The reservation model was a separate normalisation exercise. This week uses SELECT queries to read data. Activities are ungraded. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#sql-basics.

2. Columns and matching rows

Suggested time: 5 minutes

Instructional strategy: Recall and prediction

Introduce WHERE as a filter for rows satisfying a condition. Retrieve the two separate Camera items, E01 and E04. A filter changes the result, not the stored Equipment rows. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#sql-basics.

3. Two camera items

Suggested time: 6 minutes

Instructional strategy: Worked example

Expect E01 Camera and E04 Camera. Use = for equality. EquipmentDescription is a field name and Camera is the text literal. Case/collation rules depend on the DBMS and configuration; use the exact supplied value in this exercise. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#sql-basics.

4. Unreturned loans

Suggested time: 10 minutes

Instructional strategy: Teacher model with predictions

Returned uses INTEGER 0 for false and 1 for true. Expect L001, L006, L002 and L004 in the shown order. This identifies active loans, not only overdue loans. SQLite stores DueDate as valid fixed-width YYYY-MM-DD text in this starter. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#sql-basics.

5. Active loans in due-date order

Suggested time: 10 minutes

Instructional strategy: Guided paired practice

ASC means ascending, so earliest dates come first. LoanID is the second sort key if dates tie. L003 and L005 are returned, so the filter excludes them. Four active loans are stored across these dates, including dates on and after 8 April. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#sql-basics.

6. Audio equipment report

Suggested time: 12 minutes

Instructional strategy: Independent application

Use workbook question 2. SELECT EquipmentID, EquipmentDescription FROM Equipment WHERE CategoryID = 'C03' ORDER BY EquipmentID; expected E03 Recorder and E05 Microphone. Partners compare the field names, text literal, selected columns and actual result. Filtering CategoryID does not require it to appear in the selected columns. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#sql-basics.

7. A comma can change the meaning

Suggested time: 5 minutes

Instructional strategy: Misconception check with reasons

In SQLite, SELECT LoanID DueDate FROM Loan treats DueDate as an alias for LoanID, rather than selecting two fields. A statement can run and still answer the wrong question. Workbook question 7 also compares Returned with text False, which does not match this starter’s 0/1 values. Repair both the comma and the comparison. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#sql-basics.

8. The comparison matches the data

Suggested time: 5 minutes

Instructional strategy: Reflection and a fresh example

This SQLite schema restricts Returned to integer 0 or 1. The CSV and conceptual model used different representations. Use the implemented types and values rather than assuming the text False is stored. Facilities and representations vary across DBMSs. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#sql-basics.
